tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with AGENTS.md to understand the project's purpose, architecture, and conventions. This document describes the BPKPAD Document Loan Management standalone Android application, its two user roles (KASUBAG and ARSIPARIS), and the Clean Architecture pattern it follows. It provides the mental model needed before exploring any code.

tour.title: App Entry Point
tour.description: The Android app starts in MainActivity.kt, which bootstraps the application, seeds the database, and determines the start destination based on the user's role (KASUBAG or ARSIPARIS). BpkpadApplication.kt configures Hilt dependency injection and schedules the overdue loan checker WorkManager worker. The AndroidManifest.xml declares permissions, deep links, and component registration.

tour.title: Authentication & Session
tour.description: Users authenticate through the LoginScreen (Jetpack Compose UI) driven by LoginViewModel, which delegates to LoginUseCase for business logic. LoginUseCase validates credentials against the UserRepository, records the action in AuditLogRepository, and persists the session via SessionManager using Android DataStore. The OfflineAuthStore enables offline login fallback using PBKDF2 hashing and AES/GCM encryption via Android Keystore.
tour.languageLesson: Kotlin sealed classes and result types are used extensively. LoginUseCase returns a ResultState sealed class (Loading/Success/Error), enforcing exhaustive handling at each call site with no unchecked exceptions.

tour.title: Core Domain Models
tour.description: The Transaksi model is the central domain entity representing a loan transaction, with properties for status tracking, dates, PIC info, and QR token. Its status lifecycle is governed by the TransaksiStatus enum (MENUNGGU_PERSETUJUAN, DISETUJUI, DIPINJAM, DIKEMBALIKAN, DIBATALKAN, DITOLAK). Supporting models include AuditLog for immutable event records, DetailPeminjaman for document-level loan details, Perpanjangan for loan extensions, and MasterDokumen for archive document master data. These models form the vocabulary used throughout the codebase.
tour.languageLesson: Kotlin enum classes with string serialization helpers. The Transaksi model uses LocalDate for date fields with custom validation rules embedded in the domain model itself.

tour.title: Repository Contracts
tour.description: Repository interfaces define the data access contract between the domain and data layers, following Clean Architecture's dependency inversion principle. TransaksiRepository defines operations for creating, querying, approving, and canceling loan transactions. AuditLogRepository handles saving and retrieving immutable audit event records. UserRepository manages authentication and user queries. These interfaces are the boundaries through which all business logic accesses data, and they depend only on domain models, never on framework or database details.

tour.title: Transaction Business Logic
tour.description: The Use Case layer encapsulates all business logic for loan transactions. CreateTransaksiUseCase validates applicant details, phone numbers, and letter requirements, then creates and persists the transaction with audit logging. ApproveTransaksiUseCase checks that only pending transactions can be approved, generates a QR token, and records the action. RejectTransaksiUseCase requires a rejection reason. CancelTransaksiUseCase allows cancellation from pending or approved states. These use cases form the core of the domain service layer, each implementing a single `invoke` method that orchestrates validation, repository calls, and audit logging.

tour.title: Handover, Return & QR Code
tour.description: After approval, ConfirmHandoverUseCase allows the Arsiparis to mark documents as physically handed over. ReturnTransaksiUseCase processes the return of borrowed archives, validating each document's condition (BAIK, RUSAK, HILANG) and requiring damage notes when applicable. FindTransaksiByQrTokenUseCase looks up a transaction by its QR code token for quick access during return processing. The QR code is generated using ZXing via QrGenerator and shared through WhatsApp via QrShareHelper.

tour.title: Bypass Approval & Extensions
tour.description: The BypassTransaksiUseCase allows the Kasubag to directly approve a transaction with immediate effect when online approval is not possible, recording proof documentation. AcknowledgeBypassUseCase lets the Kasubag verify physical approvals that were marked as bypassed. CreatePerpanjanganUseCase manages loan extension requests, while ApprovePerpanjanganUseCase and RejectPerpanjanganUseCase handle supervisor decisions on those extensions. The AntreanApprovalScreen displays pending queues for both transactions and extensions.

tour.title: Dashboard & Transaction Form
tour.description: The UI layer provides role-specific dashboards: DashboardArsiparisScreen for archivists (transaction creation, active loans, QR scanning) and DashboardKasubagScreen for division heads (pending approvals, reports). DetailTransaksiScreen shows a comprehensive transaction view with action buttons for each workflow step. FormTransaksiScreen handles new loan submissions with document scanning and input validation via InputRules. The ScanQrScreen uses CameraX and ML Kit for barcode-based transaction lookup during returns.

tour.title: Local Room Database
tour.description: The Room database provides local SQLite persistence for offline-first operation. AppDatabase.kt configures the database with entity classes (TransaksiEntity, DetailPeminjamanEntity, AuditLogEntity, UserEntity, InstansiEntity, MasterDokumenEntity, PerpanjanganEntity) and abstract DAO getter functions. TransaksiDao defines all query and mutation operations for transactions. DatabaseModule wires the database, DAOs, and DatabaseSeeder into Hilt's dependency graph. DatabaseMigrations handles schema evolution between versions. The DatabaseSeeder populates mock data for development.
tour.languageLesson: Room uses annotation-based ORM with @Entity, @Dao, and @Database annotations. TypeConverters handle complex types like LocalDate. Entity classes mirror the domain models but add Room-specific annotations and ForeignKey constraints.

tour.title: Supabase Remote Schema
tour.description: The Supabase PostgreSQL database provides remote persistence and multi-device synchronization. The core loan_transactions table records PIC info, return plans, approval methods, and status fields. The loan_items junction table maps each transaction to specific archive documents with condition snapshots. The loan_document_locks table prevents concurrent loans of the same document. The loan_extensions table tracks extension requests with approval workflow. The loan_audit_logs table captures immutable state changes via database triggers. The LoanRemoteDataSource manages sync of all entities between Room and Supabase.
tour.languageLesson: PostgreSQL migrations use ENUM types for status fields, RLS policies for row-level security, and database triggers for automatic audit logging. Supabase syncs via RESTful PostgREST endpoints with JWT authentication.

tour.title: Reports, Network & Background Jobs
tour.description: The reports module generates Excel and PDF exports using Apache POI and Android's PdfDocument API, accessed via LaporanScreen. The network layer uses Retrofit with OkHttp, an AuthInterceptor for injecting API keys and session tokens, and SupabaseConfig for client initialization. NetworkMonitor provides runtime connectivity checks. Background tasks include OverdueWorker, a WorkManager CoroutineWorker that periodically checks for overdue loans and fires notifications via NotificationHelper. The RepositoryModule wires all repository implementations into Hilt's dependency injection graph.
